commit.message:
The cumulative form of the three- and four-point bounds

riemannzeta.fun requires the bound in cumulative windows (0, T] as well as in
dyadic windows (T, 2T], so that a submission cannot move the displayed record
by proving only a differently shaped statement. The bridge had the dyadic form
only.

No new mathematics is needed. Zeta23.cumulative_of_dyadic is generic in the
constant and in the interval-additive counting function, and
Zeta23.ThmD.thmD0_simple_mult_cumulative is built from it in four lines. These
are the same four lines with Phi_3 and Phi_4 substituted, so both cumulative
forms are unconditional exactly as the dyadic forms are, and both are added to
the standing axiom audit.

Zeta23.ThmD.Mult is already in the bridge's import chain and both files open
Zeta23 and Zeta23.ThmD, so cumulative_of_dyadic, zetaSeam, paperInputs_zeta
and N0simple_add' resolve unqualified.

Not compiled locally: the session that wrote this has no Lean toolchain. CI is
the check. Nothing has been submitted anywhere.

prime_pair_error: repair the sharp-cutoff character-weighted explicit formula

THEOREM_B_SEQUENCE.md section 3 asserts an absolutely convergent zero
expansion of I(x) = sum_{m<=x} Lambda(m) chi3(m) (x/2 - m). It is not
absolutely convergent: the coefficient (rho-1)/(2 rho (rho+1)) decays like
1/(2|gamma|), not 1/|gamma|^2, and the zero count then makes the weighted
mass diverge like log^2 T.

Adds THEOREM_B_FORMULA_REPAIR.md with a frozen candidate proposition stated
before its derivation, and the derivation itself:

- Lemma 0: I = psi_1(x,chi) - (x/2) psi(x,chi), exact.
- Proposition 3: truncated formula with the same coefficients and remainder
  C1 x^2 T^-1 log^2(xT) + 2 C1 x log x + C2, any T >= 4, from (F1) and (F2)
  alone. Endpoint convention, multiplicities and conjugate pairing carried.
- The s = -1 pole is derived, not inherited: chi3 is odd, so its trivial
  zero there collides with the kernel's 1/(s+1) and the residue is
  log x + nu with nu = euler + log(2pi/3) - 1/2 - (L'/L)(2,chi3), a double
  pole. The source document records a constant.
- Theorem 4: under an explicit isolation hypothesis (which implies GRH fails
  for chi3) plus Theta < Theta_chi, E(N_n) >> N_n^{1+2 Theta_chi} along
  x_n = exp((2 pi n - phi_0)/gamma_0), with no epsilon loss.
- Section 10 writes down the exact inequality still missing in the
  unconditional case, and why Landau's method gives the non-constructive
  epsilon-losing form instead.

Also records that the source's truncation height T = x^delta for small fixed
delta makes the error term beat the signal whenever delta < 1 - beta_0.

formula_repair_checks.py: six lightweight mpmath checks, half a second,
labelled NOT proof in the header. They pin the decomposition identity, the
trivial-zero parity, the double pole and nu, mu_1, the coefficient identity
and the 1/(2 gamma) decay at 21 located zeros, and the truncation-height
crossover.

Outcome: useful intermediate lemma plus a conditional strengthening, not a
complete sequence repair. Theorem B and the original failed argument are
unchanged. No novelty claimed, no review claimed.

Lane b78-amplification of hunt #136. Prices input I2 (Lemma 17.6, slope alpha = 5/6)
and input I9 (the direct exponent l_x/2 + b/12) in exact arithmetic, at hunt #134's
optimum and inside Liu's refined comparison system (arXiv:2610.26835v1), which is
reconstructed exactly: Liu's critical polynomial, his ell*, his kappa quartic and
his B_flat quartic are reproduced.

At hunt #134's optimum (1507 - 2 sqrt 921)/1653 the slope is worth 0.0047006135 per
unit and the direct exponent 0.8124356047; reaching 0.8748087 needs alpha =
0.8031897030 (0.8028731275 with the paper's side conditions as printed). In Liu's
system the slope is worth 0.0073713973 and reaching 0.8748087 needs alpha =
0.8229295767 at the fixed point, below Liu's stated kappa range, or 0.8229135719
inside it. 13/15 needs alpha = 0 in hunt #134's system and is out of reach of
alpha with the paper's or Liu's side conditions as stated.

Loss map: every step of the lemma is exponent-free or tight relative to its
inputs; the slope is (1 - 1/6) theta_0, the sixth power is forced (exact
enumeration in Z[w]), and theta_0 = 1 is Lemma 17.1's first width condition.
Guo's Hypothesis 11.1 is that raw moment at theta = 99/100; no arbitrary-coefficient
large sieve (Heath-Brown, Baier and Young) can give it, and on its own it implies a
zero-free half-plane Re s > 73/80. Its 328/375 is recomputed exactly; the envelope's
optimum under it is 0.8745999251.

Exact LP with dual weights, an exact decision on the whole bin rectangle, 82
citations on their lines, 37 tests. Nothing here is a result until the case log

conron_fleet: dead-man writes STOP before deleting, outlasts in-flight creates

Review of #366 (P1): at the deadline, cmd_deadman deleted VMs without
persisting RUN/STOP. Fleet.step and wait_for gate launches on STOP, not
on the deadline, so a fleet still running at its deadline could
provision replacements after the sweep and the dead-man's exit.

- stop_fleet() persists RUN/STOP; cmd_deadman calls it before its first
  delete, whichever trigger fired.
- The dead-man returns only after both providers stay empty for
  DEADMAN_QUIET_S = PROVISION_TIMEOUT_S + 120, so a create in flight
  when it fired is still swept.
- New test with a fake clock and fake providers, where a machine appears
  10 minutes after the first clean sweep: passes on the fix, fails on
  the original code at the missing STOP.

The completed 2026-10-27 run was unaffected: it ended in 4 h 6 min,
inside its 12 h deadline, and its dead-man fired on the stop file.

@@ -0,0 +1,340 @@
+# The exact-Gram rebuild of Delta_T at 280 modes (hunts/weil_propagation/c4_s2/exact_gram/).
+#
+# Ruling of 2026-10-26 (exact_gram/RUNS.md s6, s8): triggered ONLY by a push to
+# hunt/c4-exact-gram that touches exact_gram/RUN_REQUEST.json, which carries
+# the run parameters; never by this file. The request is committed only after
+# the coordinator's 'go': first {"mode": "calibrate"} once P4 closes, then the
+# full run sized from the calibration numbers.
+#
+# Jobs: plan (reads the request) -> gram (P4's G_b in gram_parts parts, gram_procs per job; G_z with
+# part 0) -> merge (sums the parts into gram.json, refusing a missing one) -> shards (each job builds the
+# disk-backed mode table once on its runner's disk, checks its size, then runs 4 worker processes
+# that stream it).
+#
+# Modes (RUN_REQUEST.json "mode"):
+#   calibrate  job 0 only, 4 processes, each `blocks` blocks of its shard; per
+#              process the per-block wall time and the peak RSS (/usr/bin/time -v)
+#              go into calibration.json in the artifact.
+#   full       shards / 4 jobs x 4 processes. The Gram is recomputed (gram and merge jobs) unless the
+#              request names a committed gram.json by "gram_sha256", which is then checked here and
+#              again by rebuild.setup (fail closed). The preflight refuses (fail closed) unless the
+#              request's "calibration" record gives at least 25 % headroom for the worst shard (its
+#              replay block priced apart) inside the 335-minute self-stop and, with the install and
+#              the table build, inside the 350-minute job limit; 4 x peak RSS < 13 GB; table < 10 GB;
+#              gram_procs x the Gram's peak RSS < 13 GB.
+#
+# 2026-10-27 (RUNS.md s12): the Gram is recomputable in full mode (the Gauss bound correction of
+# BOUNDS.md s0 changed every Gram radius); shards and jobs come from the request (88 shards of 4
+# blocks, 22 jobs, so that each runner holds exactly one dps-60 replay block); the self-stop counts
+# from job start, not from the end of the table build (the defect of RUNS.md s11.5); Gram jobs run
+# gram_procs processes (2: four peaked at 21 to 25 GiB summed in run 40342895119); only each shard's
+# last checkpoint is uploaded (assemble and resume read no other).
+name: c4-exact-gram
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - "hunt/c4-exact-gram"
+    paths:
+      - "hunts/weil_propagation/c4_s2/exact_gram/RUN_REQUEST.json"
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: c4-exact-gram
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+# GitHub runs `shell: bash` as bash -eo pipefail; a step with no shell key runs bash -e
+# without pipefail, where a failing command piped to tee passes.
+defaults:
+  run:
+    shell: bash
+
+env:
+  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
+  OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
+  OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS: "1"
+  MKL_NUM_THREADS: "1"
+  FLINT_NUM_THREADS: "1"
+  EG: hunts/weil_propagation/c4_s2/exact_gram
+
+jobs:
+  plan:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    outputs:
+      jobs: ${{ steps.p.outputs.jobs }}
+      mode: ${{ steps.p.outputs.mode }}
+      gram: ${{ steps.p.outputs.gram }}
+      gram_jobs: ${{ steps.p.outputs.gram_jobs }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - id: p
+        run: |
+          python3 - <<'PY' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          import json
+          req = json.load(open("hunts/weil_propagation/c4_s2/exact_gram/RUN_REQUEST.json"))
+          mode = req["mode"]
+          assert mode in ("calibrate", "full"), mode
+          assert req["shards"] % 4 == 0, req["shards"]
+          print("mode=" + mode)
+          print("jobs=" + json.dumps([0] if mode == "calibrate" else list(range(req["shards"] // 4))))
+          gp = req.get("gram_procs", 4)
+          assert gp in (1, 2, 4) and req["gram_parts"] % gp == 0, (gp, req["gram_parts"])
+          print("gram_jobs=" + json.dumps(list(range(req["gram_parts"] // gp))))
+          if mode == "full":  # a calibration record is required; the Gram is recomputed unless named by digest
+              assert "calibration" in req, req
+              if "gram_sha256" in req:
+                  assert len(req["gram_sha256"]) == 64, req
+          print("gram=" + ("committed" if "gram_sha256" in req else "recompute"))
+          PY
+
+  gram:
+    name: gram parts ${{ matrix.job }} (P4)
+    needs: plan
+    if: needs.plan.outputs.gram == 'recompute'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 350
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      max-parallel: 6
+      matrix:
+        job: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.gram_jobs) }}
+    steps:
+      - name: job clock (the self-stop counts from job start, RUNS.md s11.5)
+        run: echo "JOB_START=$(date +%s)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with: {python-version: "3.12", cache: pip}
+      - name: install (versions pinned in requirements.txt)
+        run: |
+          python -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check -r requirements.txt
+          python -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check --no-deps -e .
+      - name: resume (re-run attempts only)
+        if: ${{ fromJSON(github.run_attempt) > 1 }}
+        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          pattern: c4-exact-gram-gramparts-job${{ matrix.job }}-attempt*
+          merge-multiple: true
+          path: prepared/
+      - name: preflight (ball backend, snapshot guard, Gram memory)
+        run: |
+          python -c "from zeta import rigor; assert rigor.BACKEND == 'python-flint', rigor.BACKEND"
+          python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '$EG'); import guard; print(guard.key())"
+          python3 - <<'PY'
+          import json, os
+          req = json.load(open(os.path.join(os.environ["EG"], "RUN_REQUEST.json")))
+          cal = req.get("calibration") or {}
+          if "gram_peak_rss_gb" in cal:  # measured per Gram process (run 40342895119: 6.33 GiB)
+              assert req.get("gram_procs", 4) * cal["gram_peak_rss_gb"] < 13, cal
+          PY
+      - name: Gram parts
+        run: |
+          mkdir -p prepared  # attempt 1 has no download to create it (the defect of run 40342431754)
+          N=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$EG/RUN_REQUEST.json'))['gram_parts'])")
+          GP=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$EG/RUN_REQUEST.json')).get('gram_procs', 4))")
+          LEFT=$(( 335 * 60 - ($(date +%s) - JOB_START) ))
+          echo "self-stop in ${LEFT}s (335 minutes from job start)"
+          for p in $(seq 0 $(( GP - 1 ))); do
+            part=$(( GP * ${{ matrix.job }} + p ))
+            /usr/bin/time -v -o "prepared/gram_time_$part.txt" timeout "${LEFT}s" \
+              python "$EG/rebuild.py" gram-part --request "$EG/RUN_REQUEST.json" --part "$part" --parts "$N" \
+              --out prepared > "prepared/gram_log_$part.txt" 2>&1 &
+          done
+          status=0
+          for job in $(jobs -p); do wait "$job" || status=$?; done
+          tail -n 3 prepared/gram_log_*.txt
+          exit $status
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        if: always()
+        with:
+          name: c4-exact-gram-gramparts-job${{ matrix.job }}-attempt${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          path: prepared/
+          if-no-files-found: warn
+
+  merge:
+    name: merge the Gram parts
+    needs: [plan, gram]
+    if: needs.plan.outputs.gram == 'recompute'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with: {python-version: "3.12", cache: pip}
+      - name: install (versions pinned in requirements.txt)
+        run: |
+          python -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check -r requirements.txt
+          python -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check --no-deps -e .
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          pattern: c4-exact-gram-gramparts-job*
+          merge-multiple: true
+          path: prepared/
+      - name: merge (refuses a missing part or a part from another request)
+        run: |
+          N=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$EG/RUN_REQUEST.json'))['gram_parts'])")
+          python "$EG/rebuild.py" merge-gram --request "$EG/RUN_REQUEST.json" --parts "$N" --out prepared
+          sha256sum prepared/gram.json | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: c4-exact-gram-gram-attempt${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          path: prepared/gram.json
+          if-no-files-found: error
+
+  shards:
+    name: shards ${{ matrix.job }} (4 processes, ${{ needs.plan.outputs.mode }})
+    needs: [plan, merge]
+    # merge is skipped when the request names a committed Gram; a failed or cancelled merge stops the shards
+    if: >-
+      ${{ !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' && (needs.merge.result == 'success'
+      || (needs.merge.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.gram == 'committed')) }}
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 350
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      max-parallel: 6
+      matrix:
+        job: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs) }}
+    steps:
+      - name: job clock (the self-stop counts from job start, RUNS.md s11.5)
+        run: echo "JOB_START=$(date +%s)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with: {python-version: "3.12", cache: pip}
+      - name: install (versions pinned in requirements.txt)
+        run: |
+          python -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check -r requirements.txt
+          python -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check --no-deps -e .
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        if: needs.plan.outputs.gram == 'recompute'
+        with:
+          name: c4-exact-gram-gram-attempt${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          path: prepared/
+      - name: the committed Gram (named by sha256), checked fail closed
+        if: needs.plan.outputs.gram == 'committed'
+        run: |
+          mkdir -p prepared
+          cp "$EG/gram.json" prepared/gram.json
+          want=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$EG/RUN_REQUEST.json'))['gram_sha256'])")
+          got=$(sha256sum prepared/gram.json | cut -d' ' -f1)
+          echo "gram.json sha256 $got (request: $want)"
+          test "$got" = "$want"
+      - name: resume (re-run attempts only)
+        if: ${{ fromJSON(github.run_attempt) > 1 }}
+        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          pattern: c4-exact-gram-job${{ matrix.job }}-attempt*
+          merge-multiple: true
+          path: out/
+      - name: preflight (ball backend, snapshot guard, request, headroom, memory)
+        run: |
+          python - <<'PY'
+          import json, math, os, sys
+          from zeta import rigor
+          assert rigor.BACKEND == "python-flint", rigor.BACKEND
+          eg = os.environ["EG"]
+          sys.path.insert(0, eg)
+          import guard
+          k = guard.key()  # raises GuardRefused on a dirty or absent closure: fail closed
+          print("guard", k)
+          req = json.load(open(os.path.join(eg, "RUN_REQUEST.json")))
+          assert req["gram"] == "exact" and req["shards"] % 4 == 0, req
+          assert req["prepared"] == "prepared", req.get("prepared")
+          assert os.path.exists("prepared/gram.json"), "no Gram: neither recomputed nor committed"
+          if req["mode"] == "full":
+              import rebuild
+              assert hasattr(rebuild, "DiskModeTable"), "full mode needs the disk-backed mode table"
+              cal = req["calibration"]  # worst-seen prices (RUNS.md s12)
+              bl, rep = rebuild.blocks(req), req.get("replay_every") or 0
+              need = 0
+              for sh in range(req["shards"]):
+                  r = rebuild.shard_range(len(bl), sh, req["shards"])
+                  nrep = sum(1 for b in r if rep and b % rep == 0)
+                  need = max(need, (len(r) - nrep) * cal["block_wall_s"]
+                             + nrep * cal["replay_block_wall_s"] + cal["setup_s"])
+              assert need <= 0.75 * 335 * 60, f"headroom: {need:.0f} s for the worst process"
+              assert cal["table_build_s"] + need + 180 <= 0.75 * 350 * 60, f"job headroom: {need:.0f} s"
+              assert 4 * cal["peak_rss_gb"] < 13, cal
+              assert cal["table_disk_gb"] < 10, cal
+          PY
+      - name: mode table on runner disk (once per job), size checked fail closed
+        run: |
+          mkdir -p prepared out
+          SECONDS=0
+          /usr/bin/time -v -o out_table_time.txt python "$EG/rebuild.py" prepare --table-only \
+            --request "$EG/RUN_REQUEST.json" --out prepared
+          GB=$(du -sb prepared/table | awk '{print $1 / 2^30}')
+          echo "table: ${SECONDS}s, ${GB} GiB on disk" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+          python3 -c "import sys; sys.exit(0 if float('$GB') < 10 else 1)"
+      - name: run 4 shards
+        run: |
+          mkdir -p out
+          MODE=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$EG/RUN_REQUEST.json'))['mode'])")
+          SHARDS=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$EG/RUN_REQUEST.json'))['shards'])")
+          EXTRA=""
+          if [ "$MODE" = calibrate ]; then
+            EXTRA="--max-blocks $(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$EG/RUN_REQUEST.json'))['blocks'])")"
+          fi
+          LEFT=$(( 335 * 60 - ($(date +%s) - JOB_START) ))
+          echo "self-stop in ${LEFT}s (335 minutes from job start)" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+          for p in 0 1 2 3; do
+            shard=$(( 4 * ${{ matrix.job }} + p ))
+            /usr/bin/time -v -o "out/time_$shard.txt" timeout "${LEFT}s" \
+              python "$EG/rebuild.py" run --request "$EG/RUN_REQUEST.json" \
+              --shard "$shard" --shards "$SHARDS" --out out $EXTRA > "out/log_$shard.txt" 2>&1 &
+          done
+          status=0
+          for job in $(jobs -p); do wait "$job" || status=$?; done
+          tail -n 5 out/log_*.txt
+          echo "exit status $status" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+          exit $status
+      - name: calibration record (peak RSS, per-block wall)
+        if: always()
+        run: |
+          python3 - <<'PY'
+          import glob, json, re
+          rec = {}
+          import os
+          for f in sorted(glob.glob("out/time_*.txt")):
+              shard = int(re.search(r"time_(\d+)", f).group(1))
+              txt = open(f).read()
+              m = re.search(r"Maximum resident set size \(kbytes\): (\d+)", txt)
+              rec[shard] = {"peak_rss_gb": int(m.group(1)) / 2**20 if m else None}
+          for f in sorted(glob.glob("out/shard*_block*.json")):  # sorted: the last block's file carries all
+              body = json.load(open(f))
+              sh = int(re.search(r"shard(\d+)of", f).group(1))
+              rec.setdefault(sh, {})["block_seconds"] = body["payload"]["block_seconds"]
+          if os.path.exists("out_table_time.txt"):
+              m = re.search(r"Maximum resident set size \(kbytes\): (\d+)", open("out_table_time.txt").read())
+              rec["table_build_peak_rss_gb"] = int(m.group(1)) / 2**20 if m else None
+          if os.path.isdir("prepared/table"):
+              rec["table_disk_gb"] = sum(os.path.getsize(os.path.join("prepared/table", f))
+                                         for f in os.listdir("prepared/table")) / 2**30
+          json.dump(rec, open("out/calibration.json", "w"), indent=1)
+          print(json.dumps(rec, indent=1))
+          PY
+      - name: keep each shard's last checkpoint only (assemble and resume read no other)
+        if: always()
+        run: |
+          python3 - <<'PY'
+          import glob, os, re
+          files = glob.glob("out/shard*_block*.json")
+          last = {}
+          for f in files:
+              m = re.search(r"(shard\d+of\d+)_block(\d+)\.json$", f)
+              if m and (m.group(1) not in last or int(m.group(2)) > last[m.group(1)][0]):
+                  last[m.group(1)] = (int(m.group(2)), f)
+          keep = {f for _, f in last.values()}
+          for f in files:
+              if f not in keep:
+                  os.remove(f)
+          print(f"kept {len(keep)} last checkpoints, removed {len(files) - len(keep)} superseded ones")
+          PY
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        if: always()
+        with:
+          name: c4-exact-gram-job${{ matrix.job }}-attempt${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          path: out/
+          if-no-files-found: warn

@@ -0,0 +1,147 @@
+# Hunt `skewes_enclosure` (#152), production B: the 2.2e7-zero Saouter-Demichel sum.
+#
+# Each job isolates a block of 1e5-zero shards with Arb (python-flint) and
+# uploads the per-shard JSON partial sums (about 2 KB each) plus a job manifest.
+# Each shard records the SHA-256 of its zeros. Since the omega-grid rerun (B2) the
+# zeros are also uploaded, gzipped, as 90-day `zeros-*` artifacts (updated
+# 2026-10-27: this comment first said zeros were never uploaded).
+# `combine.py --target saouter_demichel` joins the 220 shards locally.
+#
+# Trigger: a push to the hunt branch that touches RUN_REQUEST.json, which names
+# the shards to run. Editing this file alone runs nothing. Never push a second
+# request while a run is running or pending: the concurrency group keeps only
+# one pending run.
+#
+# Fail-closed: the plan job validates the request (it is interpolated into a
+# shell line, so this is also the injection guard). Every job first runs a
+# smoke check against the lab box's reference and aborts on any mismatch. Each
+# block fails unless every requested shard left a sound JSON. Uploads run
+# `if: always()` so partial results survive.
+#
+# Cost (RUNS.md): 27 to 36 ms/zero near height 1e7 on the lab box, so a shard
+# takes 45 to 60 min on one core; runner speed is what the pilot measures.
+# Parallelism per job is min(nproc, floor(0.8 * MemAvailable / SHARD_RSS_KB)).
+name: skewes-enclosure
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - "hunt/skewes-enclosure"
+    paths:
+      - "hunts/skewes_enclosure/RUN_REQUEST.json"
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: skewes-enclosure-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+defaults:
+  run:
+    # GitHub's default `bash -e {0}` has no pipefail, so `check | tee` would take
+    # tee's exit status and the fail-closed gates would pass on failure.
+    shell: bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}
+
+env:
+  # Peak RSS of one 64-bit shard process near height 1e7, measured on the lab
+  # box (RUNS.md, 2026-10-26), rounded up.
+  SHARD_RSS_KB: "120000"
+
+jobs:
+  plan:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    outputs:
+      blocks: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.blocks }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - id: plan
+        run: |
+          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          import json, sys
+          req = json.load(open("hunts/skewes_enclosure/RUN_REQUEST.json"))
+          shards = req.get("shards")
+          per_job = req.get("shards_per_job", 16)
+          ok = (isinstance(shards, list) and shards
+                and all(type(k) is int and 1 <= k <= 220 for k in shards)
+                and len(set(shards)) == len(shards)

+## 6. One step of generalization, done: hunt 134's formulas against OpenAI's
+
+To price generalization with a measurement rather than a guess, the first session wrote
+hunt 134's general-geometry formulas (`hunts/seven_eighths_pin/probe.py` on its
+unlanded branch, commit `9456b4da`: `target`, `high_exponent`, `c0`, `d_x`, `p_x`,
+`r_star`, `endpoint_neg_e`) as Lean definitions over any field of characteristic zero,
+in two scratch files outside both trees, and proved them equal to OpenAI's definitions
+at the paper's point. Compiled against OpenAI's built modules, every theorem below
+reports exactly `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` *(kernel-checked, both
+sessions; source in full below)*. They are identities about formulas; none is a
+statement about zeros.
+
+| theorem | statement |
+| --- | --- |
+| `target_closed` | the matched target is 5/6 + (M - 2l)/12, for every (l, M, b) |
+| `c0_closed` | C_0 = 1/2 + l/2 - 3M/4 + b/6 |
+| `endpoint_contour_free` | at d = h the endpoint exponent does not depend on the contour, for every geometry, slope and capacity |
+| `endpoint_closed` | E_* = C_0 - δ(l + b)/2 + lxδ + (h/2)(α - δ)δP/((α - δ)D + δP) |
+| `target_paper` | the target at (1/6, 5/6, 1/8) is 7/8 |
+| `endpoint_bridge` | the general E_* at (1/6, 5/6, 1/8), slope 5/6, capacity 4/9, contour 17/50 and x = 1/2 - y is `Endpoint.balancedExponent δ y`, wherever `Endpoint.balanceDenominator δ y ≠ 0` |
+| `relative_bridge`, `source_bridge` | the general E(d) at the same point is `ProbeCentralExponent.relativeExponent`, and `sourceExponent` is 3/16 plus it |
+| `compensated_geometry_from_general` | OpenAI's `compensated_geometry` follows from a version for free (l, M, b) in which each bound is attained at d = l; an `example` elaborates OpenAI's own theorem against the same statement |
+| `gram_margin_iff` | the fourth conjunct at d = l is positive exactly when b < 3(M - 2l)/8 |

+/-- `probe.d_x` and `probe.p_x` with capacity coefficient c. -/
+def dx (c x : K) : K := 3 - (1 + 2 * c) * x

+## 7. What generalizing to symbolic parameters would take
+
+The surface numbers below are *measured* (sections 3 and 5); the effort ranges are
+*inferred*, because beyond the formula bridges of section 6 the lane generalized no
+census declaration.
+
+**Three tiers of work.**
+
+1. **Formulas.** The exponent and row-count definitions: seven in `Endpoint.lean`,
+   seven in `Hecke/DetectorRowCountCrossing.lean`, two in
+   `Hecke/InverseAmplificationBudget.lean`, two in `Detector/CentralExponent.lean`,
+   and the few other definitions of the derived class (section 5.5). Section 6 shows
+   the general forms exist, specialize by `ring`, and elaborate in seconds. Small.
+2. **Statements.** The 329 cone declarations of the union class, in 120 modules and
+   15,510 source lines, whose statements carry the constants; for example the exponent
+   literals inside `Real.rpow` in `Detector/LowSourceScales.lean`, and the structures
+   `Parameters.HighData`, `HeckeDetectorRawFiber.Fiber` and `HeckeDetectorBatch.Batch`,
+   which hold the geometry and the row counts in their fields and carry 116, 159 and 83
+   downstream declarations. 266 more cone declarations, in 190 modules, carry only a raw
+   1/6, 5/6 or 1/8 and must be read one by one, since those values have other meanings. The
+   proofs the lane read close their numeric side conditions with `norm_num`,
+   `linarith`, `nlinarith` and `positivity` at fixed numerals (inferred from
+   `Endpoint.lean`, the `Parameters*.lean` files, `Detector/CentralExponent.lean` and
+   `Detector/LowSourceScales.lean`; not counted across the census). With symbolic
+   parameters each such step needs the constraint hypotheses as inputs, and some become
+   nonlinear in the parameters.
+3. **The endpoint identity.** `Endpoint.endpoint_identity` is the paper's exact identity
+   `10368v\mathcal J(-E_*)` = (3 + 5y){(4vδ - 79)² + 49} + 4y{...} (lines 16042 to
+   16047, cited), whose integer coefficients are fixed by the geometry, the slope 5/6
+   and the capacity 4/9; `balanced_endpoint_margin` derives the 49/440640 margin from
+   it, and 20 cone declarations, including both theorems, depend on it. A symbolic
+   version needs a positivity proof for the general E_* of `endpoint_closed` that
+   holds as the parameters vary. The lane has none, and finding one is a mathematical
+   question before it is a formalization one.
+
+**Two routes.**
+
+- **Re-instantiate at one new rational point.** This is what a candidate from this hunt
+  would need. Change the constants at the census sites, compute a new exact identity
+  for the endpoint at the new numbers (exact rational arithmetic of the kind this hunt's
+  other lanes use), and rebuild. The rebuild covers every closure module
+  that imports a module with a union declaration in the cone: 1,539 of 2,924 modules,
+  8.17 hours of this build's module time, with a critical path of 47.6 minutes; after
+  an edit to `Endpoint.lean` alone it is 259 modules, 1.54 hours and 22.7 minutes;
+  after an edit to `Hecke/DetectorRowCountCrossing.lean`, 585 modules, 3.16 hours and
+  30.5 minutes *(measured from this build's log; wall times on another box would
+  differ)*. A step whose numeric side condition fails at the new point stops the build
+  at a named declaration, so the formal development doubles as a locator for where a
+  candidate breaks the argument *(inferred)*. Effort: the editing surface is the 120
+  modules above; if the numeric facts survive at the new point, days of agent editing
+  plus one or two rebuilds of about an hour each on this box; if a fact fails, the
+  lemma behind it has to be redone on paper first *(inferred)*.
+- **Symbolic parameters.** Thread a structure of parameters (l, M, b, the slope, the
+  capacity and the contour, with M + l ≤ 1 and the length inequalities of paper lines
+  8593 to 8597 as hypotheses) through the statement tier, replace the `Real.rpow`
+  exponents by expressions in it, re-prove each numeric step under hypotheses, and
+  supply the parametric positivity proof. Weeks of formalization, with that proof as

+
+**Opened 2026-10-21. Hunt #136.** The owner directed the laboratory on 2026-10-21 to
+attack RH. This hunt is the campaign's first track because a fixed zero-free half-plane
+is the RH-direct quantity the field is moving right now, and the only one whose
+argument consumes the Euler product at a named step. Nothing in this directory is a
+result until the case log in `hunts/README.md` says how it ended.
+
+Renumbering: `seven_eighths_pin/` takes #139 on main's case log (opened as #134 on `claude/hunt-134-seven-eighths-pin`); in-hunt references below still say #134.

+(algebra done here, checked in exact rational arithmetic by this hunt's tests),
+*inferred* (a reading of a paper's structure that no computation here checks),

+> OpenAI's Part II assembly by strengthening its row-count inputs, whose ceiling hunt
+> #134 places at 13/15, and (b) by a probe whose constants are not tied to the sextic
+> pole?

+  geometry with the paper's row counts held fixed gains at most 5.8e-5 (0.8749417).
+  Perfect row counts stop this assembly at 13/15.

+  Guo 0.8749570194, Liu 0.874957, Xu and Sang 0.8748867, and Liu 0.874887 for every
+  finite-order Hecke L-function over every number field, claimed optimal for that

+## Scope
+
+- **In scope.** The Part II final assembly and the lemmas that supply its row counts;

+**Hunt #136, lane `probe`, 2026-10-21, revised after two verifier passes the same day.
+Status: pricing, not proving; unreviewed by any person. Files produced, not landed:
+`probe_table.py`, `test_probe_table.py`, this page.**

+`probe_table.CITATIONS` and checked by `verify_citations` (all 91 on their stated line),
+or a line of a pinned outside source (`OUTSIDE_CITATIONS`, all 22 checked against Liu's
+cached sources and their sha256). *derived*: algebra done here, checked in exact
+rational arithmetic (fractions, and sympy for symbolic k) by `test_probe_table.py`.

+## Summary
+
+1. **The target is a function of one structural integer.** Write k for the order of the
+   row characters: the Poisson frequencies are u a^k, the signal's pole is that of
+   zeta_F(kz) at z = 1/k, and the Gram bound's exceptional frequencies are k-th powers.
+   Holding every other estimate of the paper at its stated form, the direct-bound
+   target is `sigma_0 = 1 - 1/k + (M - 2 ell)/(2k)`. The algebra is derived, symbolic in
+   k; that it describes a system whose row characters have order k rests on the k-reading
+   of item 2, so as a statement about systems it is inferred. The offset b cancels
+   exactly because the Gram coefficient 1/(2k) is half the pole: both count k-th powers.
+   At k = 6 this is hunt #134's `5/6 + (M - 2 ell)/12`.
+2. **Seven constants of the 7/8 assembly carry a 6 that this lane reads as k; the
+   sextic large sieve is not one of them.** The pole 1/6, the slot weight q_p^(-5/6),
+   the Gram term P_a^(1/6) with its two consequences b/12 and 11b/6, the amplification
+   slope 5/6 and the 6 in the plain capacity 6 kappa (section 1). Their values are cited;
+   that each 6 is the row-character order is inferred. The large-sieve exponent
+   (KD)^(2/3) is the same for every order n >= 3 (Blomer, Goldmakher and Louvel,
+   Theorem 1.3, read here from the arXiv copy; the paper follows their Section 3
+   recursion, line 4728) and enters the 7/8 only through the 11/12 bootstrap, which does
+   not bind.
+3. **Walls per k (derived, exact LPs with dual multipliers valid for every k >= 2):**
+   balanced probe `1 - 1/(2k)`, per-summand corner `1 - 3/(4k)`, and the perfect-row-count
+   floor, which depends on the floor bin. The paper's floor bin is a = 51/100,
+   delta_0 = 1/50 (line 15843), the left edge of the held Euler region x_r >= 51/100
+   that carries the nonprincipal contours (lines 4054 and 4069; that the region fixes the
+   bin is inferred); there the floor is `1 - 25/(32k)`. Hunt #134 took the limit
+   delta_0 -> 0 ("as the floor approaches 1/2"), which also needs that region extended;
+   there it is `1 - 4/(5k)`. At k = 6: 11/12, 7/8, and
+   167/192 at the paper's bin, 13/15 in the limit. So the 13/15 ceiling needs a floor
+   bin nearer 1/2 as well as perfect row counts.
+4. **With the paper's row counts carried over, every endpoint optimum is measured and
+   bracketed exactly on both sides** (section 4): an exact single-point lower bound, and
+   an exact upper bound from a point that meets every constraint of the template, the
+   endpoint by Bernstein subdivision in exact arithmetic. At k = 6 with the plain
+   capacity tied to the target the template returns 0.8749570194, the optimum Liu states
+   for this comparison system in an unrefereed arXiv preprint (2610.12234v2,

+   point xi in (0.38858, 0.38859) and his ell and b. With the capacity held at 4/9 it

+   tie. The floor rows, the Gram cap, the losslessness and the slot supply are slack
+   there, and nothing in the k != 6 structure is exercised.
+5. **Levers at k = 6, compared like for like** (variant A at the paper's floor bin,
+   measured). One step of the row order, 6 to 5, is worth 0.0255. Each other lever pushed
+   as far as the template allows: removing the Gram exceptional term outright 0.0110,
+   removing the row-count excess outright (alpha -> 0) 0.0052, the plain capacity at its

+The pole is the order of the row character, and in the paper that character is the twist
+of the completed cubic-theta sum. The paper twists by Psi(n) = Psi_0(n) prod_p

+prod chi_p(n)^(j_p)). This lane reads a candidate system as one exponent j at every

+two cited facts constrain j: the reflection's local column factor at p is
+chi_p^(-(j_p+2)) (line 1790; principal Ramanujan factors at j_p = 4, line 1791), and the

+cancels the angular factor, and the dual chi^(-3) is quadratic, which the quadratic large

+- **L1 coefficients and pairing.** Fourier coefficients of the degree-n theta at
+  squarefree indices, in closed form, with a Gauss-sum identity making (coefficient) x
+  (Gauss sum of the twist) an explicit phase that cancels the theta's angular factor.
+  *Literature* (cited from the arXiv HTML of David, Dunn, Hamieh and Lin, 2306.11875v5,
+  fetched on 2026-10-21 into scratch and read here, not in the campaign cache; quoted,
+  with the quotes normalised to ASCII): for the cubic theta "all
+  the Fourier-Whittaker coefficients were computed in closed form by Patterson [Pat77]",
+  while the quartic ones "are in general not all determined!" (section 1.2); after Hecke
+  theory and periodicity there remain
+  "n/2-1 (respectively (n-1)/2-1) undetermined coefficients" for even (odd) n (section
+  1.2); "Deligne [Del80] ... explained that the inaccessibility of the cases n>=4 on GL_2
+  was owed to the fact that local representations do not have unique Whittaker models",
+  and "Kazhdan and Patterson [KP84] generalised Deligne's work and showed the periodicity
+  property held in greater generality" (section 4.5); Suzuki's closed form covers the
+  quartic coefficients at squares m^2 of squarefree m (Remark 4.6). For n = 6 Broker and
+  Hoffstein (arXiv 1312.0568, abstract read here) give "partially proven, partially
+  conjectured values". Not known for any n >= 4.
